sentences.text: Pinacosuchus was a small crocodylomorph known for its spiky dermal armor, though only limited fossil remains exist.
Its protective suit included five distinct types of scutes, ranging from simple rectangles to elongate pointed spines.
Gilmore named the genus Pinacosuchus in 1942, establishing Pinacosuchus mantiensis as the type species.
Fossils were found in the Late Cretaceous North Horn Formation of Utah, specifically at the Lizard Locality within Manti National Forest.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as USNM 16592, includes a sacrum measuring just 14.3 mm in length.
Gilmore concluded the specimen was an adult because the neural arches of the vertebrae lacked sutures.
Taxonomically, Pinacosuchus belongs to the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically between 72.2 and 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage.
